title: The rank of a lisse sheaf is locally constant
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and put $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module sheaf [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] that is lisse: it is locally isomorphic to $E_U^{\oplus n}$, for finite $n\geq0$, on a covering of the small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site]. For $r\geq0$, let $X_r\subseteq|X|$ consist of points $x$ such that, for some (equivalently every) object $U\to X$ in a trivializing covering with $x$ in its image, $L|_U$ has rank $r$ near a preimage of $x$. This rank is independent of the trivializing covering and of the preimage. Then the $X_r$ are open and closed, only finitely many are nonempty if $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and $X=\coprod_{r\geq0}X_r$, with $L|_{X_r}$ of constant rank $r$. Each $X_r$ is given its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Choose a pro-etale trivializing covering $\{f_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ and isomorphisms $L|_{U_i}\simeq E_{U_i}^{\oplus n_i}$ with $n_i\in\mathbf N$. The index set may be infinite. This is precisely the locally free hypothesis, refining to individual finite-rank trivializations if necessary. By [sk-def-pe-site] this is an fpqc covering, in particular jointly surjective. No quasi-compactness of $X$ or of the $U_i$ is assumed here.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets

proof.text: On $W=U_i\times_XU_j$, the two trivializations induce an isomorphism $E_W^{\oplus n_i}\simeq E_W^{\oplus n_j}$: [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies each pulled-back coefficient ring with $E_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] and [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients], $\Gamma(W,E_W)=C(|W|,E)$. The isomorphism and its inverse are rectangular matrices $A,B$ over this ring: their columns are the coordinates of the images of the global standard basis sections, and their inverse identities give $AB=1$ and $BA=1$. If $w\in|W|$, evaluating entries at $w$ preserves sums and products and gives inverse $E$-linear maps $E^{n_i}\rightleftarrows E^{n_j}$. The image of the standard basis of $E^{n_i}$ is consequently a basis of $E^{n_j}$ with $n_i$ elements; comparison with its standard $n_j$-element basis using [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives $n_i=n_j$. Thus whenever $n_i\ne n_j$ the overlap $W$ is empty. This also treats rank zero, and uses no assertion that an ordinary stalk of the pro-etale coefficient sheaf is a field.

source.place: Example 3.1 (continuous-function coefficient realization); elementary matrix and basis comparison for the blueprint unit proof, paragraph 2

proof.text: For each $r\in\mathbf N$ put $W_{i,r}=U_i$ if $n_i=r$, and $W_{i,r}=\varnothing$ otherwise. These subsets and their complements are open. Their pullbacks to every $U_i\times_XU_j$ agree: if the two local ranks differ the overlap is empty by step 2, and otherwise the two pullbacks are both the whole overlap or both empty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-open-fpqc-descent] with base $S=X$, etale map $V\to S$ the identity of $X$, and covering $\{U_i\to X\}$. It gives a unique open $O_r\subseteq|X|$ with $f_i^{-1}(O_r)=W_{i,r}$. Apply the same statement to the compatible complements $U_i\setminus W_{i,r}$ to obtain an open $P_r$. Joint surjectivity shows $P_r=|X|\setminus O_r$, so $O_r$ is also closed.

source.place: Tag 03N0, lemma-open-fpqc-covering, applied with the identity etale map

proof.text: The $O_r$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $|X|$. Indeed, for $x\in|X|$, choose $u\in U_i$ above $x$ using joint surjectivity of the covering. The equality $f_i^{-1}(O_r)=W_{i,r}$ says exactly that $x\in O_r$ if and only if $n_i=r$. Thus each point belongs to exactly one $O_r$, including points where $L$ is zero (the piece $O_0$). If $X$ is empty all pieces are empty.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets

proof.text: The construction is independent of all choices. Given an additional trivializing object $V\to X$ with $L|_V\simeq E_V^{\oplus s}$, adjoin it to the chosen covering; this is still a pro-etale covering, since it retains the finite affine covering refinements of the original one. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for the enlarged family. The descended open of rank $r$ must be $O_r$, by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-open-fpqc-descent] for the original covering. Hence its preimage in $V$ is all of $V$ when $s=r$, and empty otherwise. Apply this to every constant-rank neighborhood in any trivializing covering. At every preimage of $x$ the local rank is therefore the unique $r$ with $x\in O_r$. This proves the asserted equivalence of some and every and identifies the subsets in the statement as $X_r=O_r$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets

proof.text: Give each $X_r$ its open subscheme structure. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], the maps $U_i\times_XX_r\to X_r$ form an fpqc covering; they are weakly etale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], hence form a covering of its small pro-etale site by [sk-def-pe-site]. Its nonempty members have $n_i=r$, and pulling back their trivializations using [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) gives $L|_{U_i\times_XX_r}\simeq E_{U_i\times_XX_r}^{\oplus r}$. Thus $L|_{X_r}$ is lisse of constant rank $r$. The disjoint clopen partition of step 4 gives $X=\coprod_rX_r$: the coproduct exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and its canonical map to $X$ is an isomorphism, since on each open $X_r$ it is the identity and these opens cover both schemes.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets

proof.text: If $X$ is quasi-compact, the open covering $\{X_r\}_{r\geq0}$ has a finite subcover by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Since these opens are disjoint, any $X_s$ not in that finite subcover must be empty: a point of it would also lie in a member of the subcover. Therefore only finitely many ranks occur. This argument needs no globally finite original trivializing covering.

split_report.summary: Expanded the unit rank-descent argument in seven steps, reusing only existing nodes. Compared rectangular transition matrices by evaluation to E on nonempty overlaps, descended the rank opens and their complements through the existing fpqc descent-of-opens theorem, proved independence and the scheme decomposition, and obtained finite image from quasi-compactness. Made the ambient coefficient convention and lisse meaning explicit; removed the unused coefficient-heart-closure edge (the imported cycle). No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: The entire second paragraph of the unit sk-lem-stratified-lattice proof: agreement of local ranks, open-closed saturated rank loci, fpqc descent, and reduction to constant rank. The current item markdown has the statement only; its imported proof supplies the same route.

tool_uses.why: Only the untwisted coefficient identification in clause (1), used to restrict finite free trivializations to overlaps and open rank pieces; no closure or lattice theorem is used.
HRS Example 3.1 supplies only the identification of pulled-back condensed E with continuous-function coefficients, allowing entrywise evaluation; no rank descent conclusion is imported.
Generic fpqc descent of opens, specialized to the identity etale map, is exactly the descent tool required by the unit route.
Only base-change stability ensures that the fpqc covering of each open rank piece is a pro-etale covering.
Only existence and the open/disjoint coprojections of a scheme coproduct are used to express the clopen partition as a scheme decomposition.

The statement matches the main-20261015 blueprint sk-lem-stratified-lattice-rank.md. 'Lisse' is used in the blueprint's sense of locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology (sk-lem-coefficient-heart l.11). X is any scheme, quasi-compactness is assumed only for the finiteness clause, and the statement is not weakened. The route is unit paragraph 2: clopen rank loci descend by fpqc descent of opens. Step 2: the transition matrices over C(|W|,E) satisfy AB=1 and BA=1, and evaluating at a point gives n_i=n_j by def-weil-vector-space-dimension. Γ(W,E_W)=C(|W|,E) is checked against HRS Example 3.1 p.6, which holds for any scheme. Step 3: the overlap hypothesis holds, and with V=id the node specializes exactly to Stacks 03N0 (descent.tex lemma-open-fpqc-covering); complements and joint surjectivity give clopen. Step 5: independence of choices uses only the uniqueness clause of the descent statement. Step 6: the restricted families are pro-étale coverings by 022D(3) and weakly étale base change, and the open pieces form a coproduct decomposition. Step 7: a finite subcover of a disjoint clopen cover. Edge cases tested: X empty, L=0, rank 0 against rank r, two points with ranks 1 and 2, an infinite disjoint union of points with unbounded ranks, and non-quasi-separated X. Removing the unused coefficient-heart-closure edge is justified: my transitive reachability check finds no path back to the item. An rg search of the DAG finds no duplicate. All five declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes. No fixes were made.
